user_prompt:
[TASK: ARCHITECTURAL RELIGHTING & STATIC RECONSTRUCTION]
Transform the reference photogrammetry plate into a razor-sharp, photorealistic architectural survey image.
The reference image defines the camera. Do not change the viewpoint, framing, focal length, or perspective.

MANDATORY TRANSFORMATION RULES:
1. PLANAR RECTIFICATION & GEOMETRY LOCK: Treat the reference image as an immutable spatial coordinate frame. Eliminate all 3D mesh polygon wobble, melted facades, and distorted rooflines. Plumb all vertical walls to true gravity vertical. Render the specific materials, coursing, window types, and roof forms named in the SCENE section below with sharp, correct detail.
2. STATIC DECLUTTERING (MANDATORY): COMPLETELY ERASE all transient vehicles, parked cars, delivery vans, pedestrians, and temporary street clutter from the seed image. Repaint the ground plane with the authentic surfacing, kerbs, and pavement named in the SCENE section below.
3. BOTANICAL PHENOLOGY & CANOPY INTEGRITY: Overwrite all raw 3D mesh blob foliage with authentic seasonal canopy structures matching the target date. Zero green summer foliage during dormant/autumn/winter periods:
   Vegetation consists of mature urban parkland specimens:
- *Ulmus americana* (American Elm) lining the primary avenues in broad vase-shaped habits.
- *Quercus phellos* (Willow Oak), *Quercus alba* (White Oak), and *Platanus occidentalis* (American Sycamore) distributed across open lawn sectors.
- *Acer rubrum* (Red Maple) and *Prunus serrulata* (Yoshino Cherry) occupying perimeter parklands.
- Date-grounded phenology (Early September): Dense, fully expanded late-summer deep-green canopies displaying early localized leaf-margin chlorosis, drought-induced foliage bronzing, and intact mature branch architecture. Lawn surfaces show managed aeration lines and late-summer turf wear.
4. OPTICAL DEPTH: Sharp focus across the entire frame, near to far. No blur, no depth-of-field falloff, no vignetting.

[SOLAR & ATMOSPHERIC LIGHTING OVERRIDE]
SOLAR RELIGHTING DIRECTIVE (3000K Dusk / late sunset low-angle amber golden hour with elongated cast shadows):
- SUN POSITION IN SCREEN SPACE: Sun is behind the camera and to the LEFT, out of frame (True Azimuth 276.4°, Elevation 3.7°).
- FACADE ILLUMINATION: all camera-facing facades are in full direct sunlight; left-facing walls are brightly lit and right-facing walls are in deep shadow.
- CAST SHADOW DIRECTION: cast shadows project diagonally away from the camera toward the upper-RIGHT.
- CAST SHADOW LENGTH: Cast shadows are more than twelve times the height of the object casting them: extremely long, running off the edge of the frame.
- SHADOW OVERWRITE RULE: MANDATORY: Erase every cast shadow present in the reference plate before relighting. Render all previously shadowed ground and facades as if that shadow never existed, then cast entirely new shadows so that cast shadows project diagonally away from the camera toward the upper-RIGHT. Every shadow must be angled toward the RIGHT; a shadow running straight up or straight down the frame is wrong. Do not retain, tint, or reuse any shadow from the reference plate.
- WEATHER/SKY: Crisp clear sky with direct solar exposure.

[SCENE GEOMETRY & AUTHENTIC LITHICS]
A 169.29-meter unreinforced hollow stone obelisk constructed of finely dressed Cockeysville dolomitic marble transitions visibly at the 46-meter horizontal construction seam to Massachusetts calcitic marble, terminating in a sharpened solid aluminum pyramidion apex. A concentric circular granite-paved plaza with fifty-six brushed steel flagpoles and low granite retaining walls surrounds the obelisk base. Crushed decomposed granite walkways and asphalt roadways cut through formal expanses of mown Festuca arundinacea turfgrass. The National Museum of African American History and Culture features a three-tiered inverted stepped corona clad in bronze-coated cast-aluminum filigree screens over low-E glazing. The National Museum of American History presents a rectilinear New Formalist volume of smooth-honed buff Indiana oolitic limestone with recessed bronze-framed fenestration grids. Palatial Classical Revival administrative complexes display colossal fluted limestone colonnades, deeply rusticated ashlar base courses, punched multi-pane sash windows, and hipped roofs clad in semi-cylindrical red clay Spanish tiles. An adjacent Romanesque Revival municipal building exhibits running-bond red brickwork, carved brownstone belt courses, and steep dark slate roof planes. Mature vase-shaped Ulmus americana, Quercus phellos, and Platanus occidentalis trees exhibit dense, deep-green late-summer canopies with subtle leaf-margin chlorosis.
